title: Incident entrypoint toolbar and compact brief-cards — prototype and dev review
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Design and prototype a compact "brief-cards" surface anchored to the top of incident and alert detail pages plus an 'incident entrypoint' toolbar. Goal: reduce cognitive overhead in on-call handoffs by surfacing the most actionable signals (SLO delta, recent errors, cost spike indicator, one-click runbook, postmortem links) in a single, dismissible strip and a set of small cards. This ticket covers initial high-fidelity screens, responsive behaviors, microcopy, and a developer handoff package.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype demonstrates toolbar collapsed/expanded states and three responsive widths (desktop, tablet, 320px mobile compact)
Brief-cards show SLO delta (24h), top error class, cost delta (24h), and a one-click 'Create Handoff Note' CTA in the prototype
Engineering has documented data requirements (APIs/fields) in the dev handoff doc and agreed on lazy-loading telemetry approach
PM and two on-call engineers have reviewed and provided explicit sign-off on microcopy and action discoverability
Design tokens and CSS specs exported in Figma for dev (colors, spacing, motion durations)
Prototype includes accessible keyboard focus states and aria label recommendations
design_notes: Primary constraint: surface must be compact (max 72px height collapsed), with option to expand to 280px to reveal contextual details and quick actions
We prioritized three signals to avoid noisy panels: SLO delta, error signature (linked to spans/errors dashboard), and cost per-minute delta. Additional signals move into a 'more' dropdown
Handoff composer is intentionally minimal: short textarea + attach incident link + template tags (service, priority). Templates persist per-user.
Microcopy uses active verbs and brief context: e.g., 'SLO ↓ 2.3% (24h)' and tooltips for thresholds. Avoid absolute numbers that encourage premature triage.
Mobile behavior: toolbar becomes a floating pill at bottom-right that expands into full-bleed card on tap
We will lazy-load cost telemetry to avoid adding latency to the incident page render; placeholder skeletons shown while fetching
decisions: Show only top-3 signals in the brief-cards by default to keep cognitive load low
Lazy-load cost and error details; show skeletons to preserve page speed
Use a compact 'Create Handoff Note' flow (no new modal) to reduce context switching
Expose postmortem link as a secondary action — visible only when a postmortem exists for the incident
tradeoffs: Hiding lower-priority signals reduces initial visual noise but may bury metrics some users want. Solution: 'more' menu and persistent pinning per user
Lazy-loading prevents extra latency but means some real-time signals may appear after initial triage — trade-off accepted for page load SLOs
Compact composer risks insufficient context for complex handoffs. We mitigate with templates and an 'expand to full note' option that opens incident editor
